title: CompileX
summary: A coding-contest judge where every submission is queued through Kafka, run in a sandbox and its verdict streamed back test by test.
highlights: Event-driven submission pipeline on Apache Kafka that decouples ingestion from execution and removes race conditions in evaluation.
REST APIs for submissions, profiles and leaderboards, with test-case-level verdicts pushed over WebSockets as each test finishes.
OAuth 2.0 sign-in, JWT access/refresh rotation and role-based access control; containerised with Docker to scale horizontally.
Judge0 sandboxing runs untrusted code safely across multiple languages with automated test evaluation.

title: VisionVault
summary: A photo library you search in plain English, with faces, duplicates and text in images handled automatically.
highlights: Asynchronous processing queues keep upload and search responsive at 100,000+ images.
Natural-language semantic search over vector embeddings stored in a vector database.
Backend AI pipelines for facial recognition, duplicate detection and OCR, so nothing needs manual tagging.
React interface on Node.js/Express APIs for uploading, browsing and searching.

title: OceanXray
summary: Reconstructs ocean temperature down to 1,000 m from satellite data alone, checked against real Argo float readings.
highlights: CNN encoder-decoder in PyTorch learns a 32-D latent embedding from satellite patches to predict temperature at 15 depths down to 1,000 m.
Validated against independent Argo float observations.
Python inference service with a Next.js/TypeScript dashboard for live profile visualisation.
Data pipeline turning satellite and GLORYS inputs into training-ready datasets.

title: Lyftr LLM Chat
summary: A chatbot that keeps answering when a provider fails, switching API keys on errors and serving repeat questions from cache.
highlights: LiteLLM across 2+ API keys with automatic failover on 429 and 5xx errors.
Disk and in-memory response caching; every reply reports whether it came from cache or live inference.
Endpoints for health, chat and session history, plus a header hook to simulate failures and test failover.
Whole stack starts locally with one command via Docker and a Makefile.
